We Got Christmas Presents For Our Offgrid Property! And Spend The Week Painting The Shed Floor...

Merry Christmas!

So Santa came for us and brought us a second hand toilet...
Ok, so we also got a tip trailer but hey, the toilet will be a blessing when it's required!

So in this video we prep and paint out the shed floor before filling it with our stuff! I wanted to paint my last shed floor but always said I will just do it at some stage, well soon enough the shed was so full of stuff it would have taken a week to empty it just to do the painting!
So I have jumped onto it early with this one!, I use a concrete sealing paint and it actually came out really nice so happy days!

Hope you enjoy following our little journey!

snippet.title: This Is What It Takes! Winter Living Off-Grid
snippet.description:
SunFire is the leading USA manufacturer of heaters for any shop, garage, or job site. SunFire heaters are odorless, quiet, and have no fumes and zero carbon monoxide. Visit their website at: 
https://sunfireheaters.com/influencer-landing/

Winter off-grid living in the snow belt means the work never stops.
In this video, we take you along for a real look at what it actually takes to keep everything running through deep snow, cold temps, and unpredictable winter weather.

With a rare sunny day, we clear snow off the solar panels to capture every bit of power we can — because in winter, sunlight is too valuable to waste. We also tackle essential maintenance, including snowmobile upkeep and generator checks, all necessary parts of surviving and thriving off-grid in snow country.

This isn’t staged or dramatic — it’s the daily reality of off-grid life in the snow belt:
🔹 Clearing snow from solar panels
🔹 Managing power during short winter days
🔹 Snowmobile maintenance for access and work
🔹 Generator maintenance as a backup power source
🔹 Staying ahead of winter before it gets ahead of us

Whether you’re living off-grid, planning to, or just curious about winter life beyond the grid, this video shows the maintenance and mindset required to make it through a true snow belt winter.

Thanks for being here and following along with our off-grid journey.

snippet.title: An ENTIRE Winter Off Grid | Everyday Challenges Living in Alaska
snippet.description:
Each year we brave yet another Alaskan winter, this particular season we anticipated new issues knowing we were going to experience the coldest temperatures we have ever seen. We set out to document what problems would arise and without fail things stopped working requiring us to rise to the occasion of each challenge. Although the snowy and frosted landscape can be wickedly beautiful, choosing to lead an off grid lifestyle during Alaska's coldest and darkest months can be physically demanding and psychologically difficult. Nonetheless, we are happy to have pulled through to the other side and we are left eagerly anticipating the arrival of break up season! 

We appreciate you tagging along for our Alaskan adventure 😀

Thank you for watching and supporting our channel! 💙

snippet.title: Our GENERATOR DIED… So We Finished Our GIANT Solar System || Off Grid Cabin Life in Alaska
snippet.description:
Our primary generator blew the head gasket. Repair cost as much as a new one — and there was no more money in the budget. So we did the only thing we could: we finally finished the giant solar system we started last summer.

In this video, we mount the last solar panels, wire the battery bank, connect the inverter charger, troubleshoot a bad connector that took down half the array, and fire the whole system up for the first time. 

With a little help from two friends — one off grid Alaska veteran and one former Coast Guard electrical technician — we got it done.

Two weeks later update: we haven't run the generator once.

This system was designed for our family of nine by the team at Santan Solar. If you're thinking about solar for your home or off grid setup, check the link below — they'll help you design a system for your specific needs.

What's in Our System:

20x 400-watt solar panels (8,000-watt PV array)
EG4 battery bank system
Heavy-duty inverter/controller
Custom designed for off-grid family life

Thanks to Santan Solar for helping us design this system and sponsoring this series! They'll help anyone design their perfect solar setup, whether you're off-grid or need backup power.

snippet.title: No Grid Power Needed to Live Your Life! | Off-Grid Homestead
snippet.description:
Join us for an exciting look at an amazing off grid cabin, complete with modern amenities for comfortable off grid living. We explore the impressive solar panels powering this setup, ensuring a sustainable energy source. This cabin tour showcases a truly self-sufficient homesteading experience.

Truly impressive solar system runs this entire homestead with ease, with over 8.6kw of solar panels, 28kw of lithium battery storage, and 12k watts of pure sine wave inverter output, power is not going to be a problem!

7,000 gallons of water storage ensure you never run out of necessary water, and with a a sediment filter, 3 filter housing, UV light filter, and countertop gravity fed filter clean water is ensured. 

Large 500 gallon propane tank will supply the necessary fuel for 2yrs+ on this off grid homestead, thus reducing your need for outside resources, and giving you time to convert more things to run off the excess solar power, or install wood heating options!

Plenty of room for a garden, livestock and privacy, this type of set up is getting harder to find each day.

snippet.title: Off Grid Couple's Island Build | The Excavation That Changed Everything
snippet.description:
*MY WILD HOLM S4 Ep16* — Off Grid Couple's Island Build | The Excavation That Changed Everything!

⚠️ *IMPORTANT SAFETY & EDUCATIONAL CASE STUDY*⚠️
*DO NOT ATTEMPT TO COPY, REPEAT, ADAPT, OR REPLICATE THIS BUILD.*

_This video is being left online strictly as a documentary case study and safety warning. It shows earlier footage from our project before we fully understood the serious engineering risks involved in underground excavation._

The excavation methods shown in this video were unsafe. Unshored or improperly supported earth can collapse without warning. A cave-in can trap, crush, suffocate, or kill a person in seconds. Heavy equipment, loose soil, water, vibration, spoil piles, depth, and changing ground conditions can all increase the danger.

We now understand that underground construction and excavation require proper professional assessment, engineering guidance, permits, and compliant protective systems such as engineered shoring, sloping, benching, or shielding where required.  There are a few bunker episodes already filmed that still show that phase of the work. We’re about four months behind real time in production. What you’re seeing now was shot earlier in the season. Going forward, the excavation will be properly sloped, benched, or reinforced before I step back inside. Lesson learned.

----------

*CHAPTERS*
00:00 *Safety Warning — Do Not Replicate*
This video is shared as a documentary safety warning, not as a method or tutorial.

00:10 – *How This All Started*
We bought the island sight unseen.

04:28 *Airport Boots & Travel Hurdles*
Melodi dealing with heavy work boots and airline baggage limits.

08:39 *New Tools & Moving Gear Around*
Assembling the Gorilla cart and reorganizing heavy supplies.

11:43 *Equipment Inside an Unsafe Excavation*
Operating equipment inside an unprotected excavation creates serious risk and should not be replicated.

13:04 *Power Setup & Cabin Work Continues*
Using Bluetti power and finishing work on the cabin front.

20:31 *Garden & Landscape Walkthrough*
Checking plantings, lavender, soil progress, and sitting areas.

23:51 *The Big Dig*
Discussing the excavation issues and next steps.

🛑 *CRITICAL SAFETY ISSUES SHOWN*
This video includes unsafe excavation, lack of professional shoring or engineered protection, equipment operating inside an excavation, and work near unsupported soil.

The bunker scenes in this video are not instructions. They are shown only as part of the documentary timeline and as a warning about what not to do. We have since changed our approach and are following proper safety protocols.

📘 *SAFETY RESOURCES*
Before any excavation or underground build, consult qualified professionals and your local regulations.

• WorkSafeBC excavation and shoring requirements
• CCOHS trenching and excavation safety guidance
• OSHA trenching and excavation safety guidance
• A licensed geotechnical / structural engineer
• Local building department and permit authority

We are sharing this because we learned from it, not because it should be repeated.

----------

While Melodi is away, Ryan keeps things moving and our off grid island build continues.  We've learned alot during this process and in the end, this excavation actually changed everything.  We had no idea of the dangers associated with it and have sure learned our lesson. Small projects add up. Soil gets amended. A compost tumbler goes together so we can start learning what works in this climate. 🪱🪵A heavy-duty dump cart arrives to help move material across uneven ground without wearing ourselves down. 🛠️

Melodi returns to the island and we take stock of how things are growing and changing. Some fruit didn’t make it. The garden shows promise. New plantings are settling in and we adjust as we go. 🍓🍇
We also continue a major new project... a below-grade battery bunker designed to protect our solar power system through winter. ❄️🔋 

As always, progress here comes from steady effort. Not everything works the first time. Adjustments are constant. Over time, those small decisions turn into something solid. 💪 This is off grid life as it actually unfolds. Quiet work. Practical choices. One step at a time. 🌅

If you’re new here, start at the beginning and follow the full journey of building our remote island homestead.

snippet.title: Life in Oregon's Hidden Off-Grid Community | Unpaved: Respite from the World (Documentary, 2023)
snippet.description:
A hauntingly beautiful farmland, hidden somewhere in Oregon's mountains, is home to horses and dogs, ex-cons and ex-addicts, drummers, dreamers and Bigfoot hunters. Steve is a kind-hearted landlord who allows his renters to be late with the rent - or not pay rent at all. Amber is the woman Steve can't stop loving, even when she betrays him. Buzz isolates himself in a tent, nurturing dreams of an expedition with his mule. Ron spent a decade in prison and now dwells in a forest cabin with Gale, whose father is suddenly rushed to hospital. Tom Junior has conquered the meth addiction that killed his brother and is now patiently cooking food for Tom Senior. The passionate drummer Sky is convinced that Bigfoot hides in the woodlands. Mikael Lypinski approaches this nonconformist village with curiosity and a deeply felt humanism, capturing poetic, humoristic moments in the lives of its characters. Unpaved is a patchwork of interweaving stories and destinies, offering a moving insight into off-grid America, where people have turned their backs to society to live in sync with nature. Unpaved is the second part of an American trilogy of documentaries by Mikael Lypinski portraying an unknown, unmanicured part of the USA. The first part was the award-winning "Desert Coffee", set in Slab City in southern California. 

Watch the documentary "Desert Coffee" here: https://youtu.be/IfFYDBAgFQ8
